bottom_line: Diet plus pravastatin vs diet alone reduced coronary heart disease (66 events vs 101 events; HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.49–0.91).
implications: In this trial of diet vs diet plus pravastatin in Japanese patients with hypercholesterolaemia, the primary endpoint (coronary heart disease) occurred less often with pravastatin (66 vs 101 events; HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.49–0.91). The data support a reduction in coronary heart disease events over mean follow-up 5.3 years; they do not show a statistically significant difference for stroke at end of study (HR 0.83, 0.57–1.21) or for total mortality at end of study (HR 0.72, 0.51–1.01).

major_points.text: Prospective, randomised, open-labelled, blinded-endpoint trial in hypercholesterolaemia with no history of coronary heart disease or stroke.
major_points.quote: In this prospective, randomised, open-labelled, blinded study, patients with hypercholesterolaemia (total cholesterol 5·69–6·98 mmol/L) and no history of coronary heart disease or stroke were randomly assigned diet or diet plus 10–20 mg pravastatin daily.

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was first occurrence of coronary heart disease.
major_points.quote: The primary endpoint was the ﬁrst occurrence of coronary heart disease.

major_points.text: Randomised allocation: 3966 to diet and 3866 to diet plus pravastatin; mean follow-up 5.3 years.
major_points.quote: 3966 patients were randomly assigned to the diet group and 3866 to the diet plus pravastatin group. Mean follow-up was 5·3 years.

major_points.text: Coronary heart disease events were lower with diet plus pravastatin than diet alone.
major_points.quote: Coronary heart disease was signiﬁcantly lower in the diet plus pravastatin group than in the diet alone group (66 events vs 101 events; HR 0·67, 95% CI 0·49–0·91; p=0·01).

major_points.text: No difference reported in malignant neoplasms or other serious adverse events between groups.
major_points.quote: There was no diﬀerence in the incidence of malignant neoplasms or other serious adverse events between the two groups.

major_points.text: Lipid reductions differed between groups over follow-up (mean total cholesterol and LDL cholesterol).
major_points.quote: Mean total cholesterol was reduced by 2·1% (from 6·27 mmol/L to 6·13 mmol/L) and 11·5% (from 6·27 mmol/L to 5·55 mmol/L) and mean LDL cholesterol by 3·2% (from 4·05 mmol/L to 3·90 mmol/L) and 18·0% (from 4·05 mmol/L to 3·31 mmol/L)

absolute_effects.text: Coronary heart disease: 101 (5.0) vs 66 (3.3) (events per 1000 person-years).
Number needed to treat (NNT) to prevent one coronary heart disease event was 119 during average 5.3 years follow-up.
absolute_effects.quote: The number needed to treat (NNT) to prevent one coronary heart disease event was 119 during the average 5·3 years follow-up.

absolute_effects.text: Absolute risk reduction for coronary heart disease was 0.8% (95% CI 0.2–1.5).
absolute_effects.quote: the absolute risk reduction was 0·8% (95% CI 0·2–1·5).

subgroups.text: Subgroup analyses assessed interactions between treatment and prognostic factors including sex, age, lipid concentrations, diabetes, hypertension, BMI, and smoking.
subgroups.quote: The Cox’s proportional hazards model was used to identify clinically relevant interactions between treatment and prognostic factors, including sex, age, total cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol, and triglyceride concentrations, diabetes, hypertension, body-mass index, and whether the patient was a current or past smoker.

subgroups.text: No significant interactions in any subgroup for risk reduction of coronary heart disease.
subgroups.quote: Subgroup analysis of the risk reduction of coronary heart disease with pravastatin did not show signiﬁcant interactions in any subgroup (ﬁgure 4).

harms.text: No difference in incidence of malignant neoplasms or other serious adverse events between groups.
harms.quote: There was no diﬀerence in the incidence of malignant neoplasms or other serious adverse events between the two groups.

harms.text: No rhabdomyolysis occurred in either group.
harms.quote: No rhabdomyolysis occurred in either group (data not shown).

harms.text: Aminotransferase elevations >100 IU/L were reported with counts in both groups.
harms.quote: aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase concentrations exceeded 100 IU/L in 55 (1·4%) and 104 (2·8%) of 3729 patients, respectively, in the diet group and 50 (1·3%) and 107 (2·8%)

harms.text: Abnormal creatine kinase concentrations (>500 IU/L) were reported with counts in both groups.
harms.quote: Abnormal creatine kinase con- centrations (>500 IU/L) were seen in 98 (2·6%) of 3738 patients in the diet group and 111 (3·1%) of 3629 patients in the diet plus pravastatin group

guidelines_referenced.text: National Cholesterol Education Program step I diet
guidelines_referenced.quote: Patients in both groups were counselled to follow the National Cholesterol Education Program step I diet.15

guidelines_referenced.text: Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare regulations for postmarketing surveillance
guidelines_referenced.quote: The trial was done in compliance with the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare regulations for postmarketing surveillance.

inclusion_criteria.text: Men and postmenopausal women aged 40–70 years with bodyweight of 40 kg or more and hypercholesterolaemia (total cholesterol concentration 5.69–6.98 mmol/L).
inclusion_criteria.quote: Brieﬂy, men and postmenopausal women aged 40–70 years with a bodyweight of 40 kg or more and hypercholesterolaemia (total cholesterol concentration 5·69–6·98 mmol/L) were eligible

exclusion_criteria.quote: Major exclusion criteria were familial hypercholesterolaemia

exclusion_criteria.text: History of coronary heart disease or stroke.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Major exclusion criteria were familial hypercholesterolaemia and a history of coronary heart disease or stroke.

analysis_methods.text: Analyses done by intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: Statistical analyses were done by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: Sample size of 8000 planned for >80% power with α=0.10 (two-sided) and assumed 20% dropout.
analysis_methods.quote: A sample size of 8000 individuals would have more than 80% power with α=0·10 (two-sided) and an assumed 20% dropout.

analysis_methods.text: Hazard ratios and CI estimated using Cox proportional hazards model.
analysis_methods.quote: Hazard ratios and CI were estimated with the Cox’s proportional hazards model.

analysis_methods.text: Three interim analyses were done (September 2000, 2001, 2002) per predefined statistical analysis plan.
analysis_methods.quote: Three interim analyses were done in September, 2000, September, 2001, and September, 2002, in accordance with the predeﬁned statistical analysis plan.

trial_conduct.quote: This trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov, number NCT00211705.

trial_conduct.text: Written informed consent obtained from outpatients meeting inclusion criteria.
trial_conduct.quote: Written informed consent was obtained from outpatients who met all the inclusion criteria.

trial_conduct.text: Trial conducted in compliance with Declaration of Helsinki and Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare regulations for postmarketing surveillance.
trial_conduct.quote: The trial was done in compliance with the ethical principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare regulations for postmarketing surveillance.

trial_conduct.text: Data and safety monitoring committee recommended continuing study for additional 5 years to increase number of events.
trial_conduct.quote: on the basis of recommendations from the data and safety monitoring committee, the study was continued for an additional 5 years to increase the number of events.

trial_conduct.text: Independent data centre monitored total cholesterol concentrations and alerted physicians when high.
trial_conduct.quote: An independent data centre monitored the total cholesterol concentrations of all patients and alerted physicians if a patient’s total cholesterol was high;

funding_declarations.text: Sponsor had no role in study design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, or writing.
funding_declarations.quote: The sponsor of the study had no role in study design, data collection, data analysis, data interpretation, or writing of the report.

funding_declarations.text: Initial funding by Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare; later funded by Sankyo Co Ltd, Tokyo.
funding_declarations.quote: Research funds were provided by the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare for the ﬁrst 2 years of the study, and thereafter the study was funded by Sankyo Co Ltd, Tokyo.

funding_declarations.text: Authors received travel grants or speaking honoraria from Sankyo; one author had stock in Sankyo; several received lecture fees from Sankyo or from Merk-Banyu and Pfizer Japan.
funding_declarations.quote: All authors have received travel grants or speaking honoraria from Sankyo Co Ltd for this study. K Arakawa has stock in Sankyo.

criticisms.text: Possibility that stroke result at 5 years could be due to chance.
criticisms.quote: However, for stroke, the possibility of a chance outcome cannot be ruled out.

criticisms.text: High statin uptake in diet-only group after 5 years could make intention-to-treat outcomes more conservative.
criticisms.quote: The high uptake rate after 5 years for statin use in those assigned diet only could have resulted in more conservative outcomes in this intention-to-treat analysis.
